The work around teaching

A good program needs more
than a meeting link.

You also need a way to reach seekers, explain the offer, and keep everything organised.

01

Getting found

Posting about your skill does not always help people understand what they can learn from you or how to book.

02

Answering the same questions

People need to know the level, schedule, materials, and price. Repeating those details in separate messages takes time.

03

Keeping track of the program

Enrollments, messages, files, and session links can end up in different places when you manage them separately.

Be part of a learning marketplace

Help seekers understand
what you can teach them.

Your public profile puts your background, skills, languages, and portfolio alongside your programs. Seekers can search for programs or look for a provider by name.

Each program explains the outcomes, level, requirements, and schedule. This gives people useful information before they decide to book or send you a question.

After a completed enrollment, a seeker can leave a review. You can respond publicly, so future seekers can read both the feedback and your reply.

Your public profile

Show what is relevant to your subject

  • Professional and teaching experience
  • Skills, languages, and relevant qualifications
  • A portfolio with images, video, audio, or documents
  • Your programs and available seeker reviews
From idea to program

Explain the offer clearly.
Set the terms yourself.

Choose the format, level, price, capacity, and schedule. Tell seekers what they will practise and what they need to bring. Save a draft and return to it when you are ready.

If writing the listing slows you down, describe the idea in a sentence. The optional AI writing assistant can suggest a title, description, and details supported by your prompt. Review and edit the result before publishing, or write everything yourself.

When you run a program again, add more start dates or duplicate it into a new draft. Repeating dates in a series share announcements, discussion, and one resource library.

Example program draft
“A live online sketching program for beginners.”
Review and edit before publishing

Beginner Sketching Program Online

Explain the exercises you will cover, the materials seekers need, and what they will practise.

BeginnerOnlineWorkshop format

Illustrative draft. You choose the final details.

Run the program in one place

Keep the admin
with the learning.

Use the provider dashboard to manage programs, find enrolled seekers, check the calendar, and reply to messages. Reports show enrollments, reviews, and earnings for the dates you choose.

For an online session, start the built-in video room from the schedule. Share your screen, follow the session chat, and check seekers in. Upload supporting resources to the program so enrolled seekers can find them afterward.

  • Send official updates through announcements.
  • Keep group questions in program discussion.
  • Use private messages for individual questions.

Becoming a provider

Start with your application.

01

Tell us about your experience

Apply from your account. Add your bio, background, skills, languages, and relevant qualifications or portfolio links.

02

Receive a review decision

talent-share reviews provider applications. You are notified by email when your application is submitted and when a decision is made.

03

Prepare your first program

Once approved, create your program, check the details, and publish it. Your profile and program help seekers decide whether to book.

Before you apply

Provider questions

You can learn as a seeker and apply to become a provider with the same account.

What do I need to apply to teach?

Prepare a profile photo, bio, professional background, skills, and the talents you want to share. Add relevant education, certifications, teaching experience, languages, and links. The application shows required information that is missing before you submit it for review.

Can I create a program without using AI?

Yes. You can fill in the program details yourself. If you use the writing assistant, start with a short description of your idea, then check and edit the suggested listing before publishing. You choose the final content, schedule, price, and capacity.

How do providers manage their programs?

The provider dashboard brings together drafts and published programs, seeker lists, the teaching calendar, program messages, and reports. Providers can see enrollment and earnings information and export reports for a selected date range.

Can I teach and learn with the same account?

Yes. You can learn with your account and apply to become a provider from it. After approval, your teaching and learning activity have their own dashboard views under the same login.
